x: Kopra Reservoir is Chhattisgarh's first Ramsar site. AP's only Ramsar site is Kolleru (2002), India's first was Chilika (1981), and Kopra has no link to Odisha.

Laterite, peaty and forest soils are generally acidic. Black soil and saline-alkaline soils are neutral to alkaline, and arid, alluvial and red soils are not listed as acidic, so every other group includes a non-acidic soil.

Mining-led deforestation is linked to Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Punjab, Haryana and western UP suffer from over-irrigation, and Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra from overgrazing.
Most of Andhra Pradesh's iron ore is haematite, and Anantapur ranks first in the State for iron ore. Magnetite has the most iron, but it is not AP's main ore; limonite and siderite are lower grades.

Keonjhar and Bonai in Odisha are iron-ore areas. Sundargarh and Kendujhar are manganese areas (not copper), Balaghat and Chhindwara are MP manganese areas (not chromite), and Zawar near Udaipur is lead-zinc (not manganese).

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: in July 2026 the SC upheld the Centre's royalty formula, based on an Average Sale Price that includes royalty, DMF and NMET. Statement 3 is wrong: royalty is not a tax, as held in MADA v. SAIL (2024).

GoAP gives the area of AP as 1,62,970 sq km (about 4.96% of India). 1,60,205 sq km is an older post-bifurcation base figure, not the area at formation; 2,75,000 sq km was undivided AP; 1,30,060 sq km is unrelated.
